Credit: Zoë Takaki Juan Muñoz, Oak Park Township trustee and owner of Sugar Fixé, recently joined 14 other Illinois residents in a lawsuit against the federal government for alleged misconduct by immigration enforcement agents last year.   This is just one of the legal battles Muñoz’ has fought since last fall while also leading as a local government official, running a local business, and most importantly to him, doing what is best for his family as a father of three.   “It’s been a year of really trying to understand what my role is, one, as a representative of the community, but then also to use the situation I was put in to try to seek accountability and limit the harm that’s happening,” said Muñoz.   In addition to legal action, he also participated in the HART Truth-Telling Commission earlier this year, to record the incidents that occurred and continue to pursue accountability.   “It’s important to continue to give voice to the communities that are not able to show up and have too much of a risk, too much at stake, to be able to show up themselves,” said Muñoz. “In the past, especially growing up in small communities, there was a silence when immigration raids happened, when workplace audits happened, and people disappeared. That silence has its own arm, that it does not lead to change.”  He said there is also a need to move forward and heal, even as accountability is pursued. Muñoz not only had to learn the federal legal system, but how to balance his life and responsibilities with the new reality that he was “thrust into.”   Earlier in 2025, Muñoz became an owner of Sugar Fixé in downtown Oak Park. About the Author Scott Blackburn is the Institute for Free Speech’s Research Director, a position he has held since 2018. He is responsible for spearheading the Institute’s short-term and long-term research efforts on the regulation of free political debate and free association and played a major role in authoring and publishing the organization’s first Free Speech Index in March 2018, which graded the 50 states on their political giving freedom. Blackburn’s primary areas of research expertise include campaign spending, internet speech regulations, political contribution limits, disclosure mandates, the Federal Election Commission, the Supreme Court’s campaign finance jurisprudence, and other speech-related regulations at both the federal and state level. His writing has appeared in numerous publications, including *The Wall Street Journal*, *USA Today*, and the *New York Post*. Blackburn originally joined the Institute in June 2014. Prior to joining the Institute for Free Speech, Blackburn worked at the Cato Institute, the American Action Forum, and wrote for the political fact-checking website, FactCheck.Org. He graduated from the University of Pennsylvania with a B.A. in Political Science in 2012. A Cleveland native, Blackburn is husband to his loving and supportive wife, Katie, and the proud father of two young children, three-year-old Declan and one-year-old Charlotte.
